Passing the **NCLEX (National Council Licensure Examination)** requires a structured study plan, consistent practice, and a deep understanding of nursing concepts. Below is a **comprehensive to-do list** to help you prepare effectively.

---

### **📌 NCLEX Prep To-Do List**
#### **📅 Phase 1: Assessment & Planning (1-2 Weeks)**
✅ **Understand the NCLEX Format**
- Review the **NCLEX test plan** ([NCSBN website](https://www.ncsbn.org/nclex.htm)).
- Know the **categories** (Safe & Effective Care Environment, Health Promotion, Psychosocial Integrity, Physiological Integrity).
- Understand **question types** (Multiple-choice, Select-all-that-apply, Hot spots, Drag-and-drop, Fill-in-the-blank).
- Learn about **NCLEX scoring** (Computer Adaptive Testing - CAT).

✅ **Take a Diagnostic Test**
- Use **UWorld, Kaplan, or Saunders** to take a **baseline assessment**.
- Identify **weak areas** (e.g., Pharm, Delegation, Prioritization, Maternity, Psych).
- Set a **target score** (aim for **60-70%+** on practice tests).

✅ **Set a Study Schedule**
- **Ideal timeline:** **4-8 weeks** of dedicated study (adjust based on your diagnostic score).
- **Daily study time:** **3-6 hours/day** (with breaks).
- Use a **planner or digital tool** (Google Calendar, Notion, Trello).
- **Example Schedule:**
  - **Morning (2-3 hrs):** Content review (weak areas)
  - **Afternoon (1-2 hrs):** Practice questions (50-100/day)
  - **Evening (1 hr):** Review incorrect questions + notes

✅ **Gather Study Materials**
- **Primary Resources:**
  - **UWorld** (Best for practice questions & rationales)
  - **Saunders Comprehensive Review** (Great for content)
  - **Kaplan NCLEX Prep** (Good for strategies)
  - **Mark Klimek Lectures (Audio)** (High-yield for Pharm & prioritization)
  - **Simple Nursing / RegisteredNurseRN (YouTube)** (Visual learners)
- **Secondary Resources:**
  - **NCLEX High Yield Podcast**
  - **Nurse Achieve / Hurst Review** (If available)
  - **Anki Flashcards** (For memorization)

✅ ** Join a Study Group (Optional)**
- Find a **focused, motivated group** (online or in-person).
- Use **Discord, Facebook groups, or Reddit (r/NCLEX)** for support.

---

#### **📚 Phase 2: Content Review (3-6 Weeks)**
✅ **Focus on High-Yield Topics** (Prioritize based on your weak areas)
- **🩺 Pharmacology** (Most heavily tested!)
  - **Must-know meds:** Insulin, Anticoagulants (Heparin, Warfarin), Antibiotics, Antihypertensives, Diuretics, Chemo drugs, Psych meds (Lithium, SSRIs, Antipsychotics).
  - **Side effects, nursing considerations, patient teaching.**
  - **Mark Klimek’s Pharm Audio** (Gold standard!)
- **🩹 Fundamentals & Skills**
  - **Safety (Infection control, restraints, falls prevention)**
  - **Delegation & Prioritization (Who to see first? What to delegate to LPN/CNA?)**
  - **Legal & Ethical (Informed consent, HIPAA, advance directives)**
  - **IV Therapy, Blood Transfusions, TPN, NG Tube Care**
- **👶 Maternity & Pediatrics**
  - **Prenatal care, labor stages, complications (Preeclampsia, Eclampsia, Placenta Previa, Abruptio Placentae)**
  - **Newborn care (Apgar, hypoglycemia, jaundice, congenital disorders)**
  - **Growth & development milestones**
- **🧠 Psychiatric Nursing**
  - **Therapeutic communication, crisis intervention, suicide risk, hallucinations/delusions**
  - **Mood disorders (Depression, Bipolar), Schizophrenia, Anxiety, Personality Disorders**
  - **Restraints & seclusion (least restrictive first)**
- **💓 Medical-Surgical (Most Common NCLEX Questions!)**
  - **Cardiac (MI, Heart Failure, AFib, Pacemakers, Telemetry Interpretation)**
  - **Respiratory (COPD, Asthma, ARDS, Mechanical Ventilation)**
  - **Endocrine (Diabetes, DKA, SIADH, DI, Thyroid disorders)**
  - **Neurological (Stroke, Seizures, TBI, Meningitis, Parkinson’s, Alzheimer’s)**
  - **Renal (AKI, CKD, Dialysis, Fluid & Electrolytes)**
  - **GI (Liver Cirrhosis, Pancreatitis, Cholecystitis, Bowel Obstruction)**
  - **Oncology (Chemo side effects, radiation, pain management)**
- **🩸 Lab Values & Nursing Implications**
  - **Critical labs:** K+ (3.5-5.0), Na+ (135-145), Ca2+ (9-10.5), Mg (1.5-2.5), Glucose, ABGs, INR/PTT, Hgb, Hct, WBC.
  - **What to do if abnormal?** (e.g., High K+ → Kayexalate, Insulin + D50, Albuterol)
- **🚨 Emergency & Critical Care**
  - **Shock (Types, S/S, Treatment)**
  - **Sepsis (SBAR, Early recognition, Fluids, Antibiotics)**
  - **Burns (Rule of 9s, Fluid resuscitation, Complications)**
  - **Poisoning/Overdose (Antidotes: Narcan, Digibind, Protamine, Vitamin K)**

✅ **Use Active Learning Techniques**
- **Summarize notes** in your own words.
- **Teach concepts** to a friend or imaginary audience.
- **Draw diagrams** (e.g., cardiac conduction system, insulin action).
- **Make mnemonics** (e.g., **"Haldol + Benadryl + Cogentin"** for EPS symptoms).
- **Flashcards** (Anki or handwritten) for meds, lab values, and key concepts.

✅ **Daily Practice Questions (50-100/day)**
- **UWorld is KING** (Do all 2,000+ questions if possible).
- **Review every question** (even the correct ones) – **rationale is GOLD**.
- **Flag & re-review** difficult questions weekly.
- **Track progress** (Aim for **65%+** in practice tests).

---

#### **🎯 Phase 3: Test-Taking Strategies (Ongoing)**
✅ **Master NCLEX-Style Questions**
- **Identify the "stem" (what is the question really asking?)**
- **Look for "priority" words** (First, Best, Most, Immediately).
- **Eliminate wrong answers first** (ABCs: Airway, Breathing, Circulation).
- **Watch for absolutes** ("Always, Never, Only" → Usually wrong).
- **For Select-All-That-Apply (SATA):**
  - Assume **all options are correct** unless you can prove otherwise.
  - If you can justify **2-3 answers**, pick those.
  - **No partial credit** – only all correct or all wrong.

✅ **Prioritization & Delegation**
- **Maslow’s Hierarchy** (Physiological > Safety > Love/Belonging > Esteem > Self-Actualization).
- **Nursing Process (ADPIE)** – **Assess before implement!**
- **Who to see first?**
  - **Unstable vs. Stable** (e.g., Chest pain > Routine med admin).
  - **Acute vs. Chronic** (e.g., New-onset SOB > Long-term diabetes management).
- **What to delegate?**
  - **LPN:** Stable patients, med administration, vital signs.
  - **CNA:** ADLs (bathing, feeding, ambulation).
  - **RN cannot delegate:** Assessments, evaluations, critical patients.

✅ **Time Management**
- **Pace yourself:** ~1.5 min per question (you have **6 hours for 75-265 questions**).
- **Flag & move on** if stuck (don’t spend >3 min on one question).
- **Take breaks** (After 60, 120, 180 questions – stretch, hydrate, snack).

---

#### **🏆 Phase 4: Final Review & Test Simulation (Last 1-2 Weeks)**
✅ **Full-Length Practice Tests (3-5 in total)**
- Simulate **real test conditions** (timed, no distractions).
- **UWorld Self-Assessment Tests** (Predicts likelihood of passing).
- **Kaplan/ATI practice exams** (If available).
- **Review all mistakes thoroughly** (Why was I wrong? What did I miss?).

✅ **Focus on Weak Areas**
- Revisit **lowest-scoring topics** from practice tests.
- **Drill SATA questions** (Many students struggle with these).
- **Prioritization/Delegation drills** (Use **La Charity or UWorld** books).

✅ **Memorize Key Mnemonics & Charts**
- **Insulin types (Onset, Peak, Duration)**
- **Critical Lab Values**
- **ABG Interpretation (ROME: Respiratory Opposite, Metabolic Equal)**
- **IV Fluids (Isotonic, Hypotonic, Hypertonic)**
- **Electrolyte Imbalances (S/S & Treatments)**

✅ **Mental & Physical Prep**
- **Sleep:** **7-8 hours/night** (especially the week before).
- **Exercise:** Light activity (walking, yoga) to reduce stress.
- **Nutrition:** Eat brain foods (omega-3s, nuts, berries, dark chocolate).
- **Hydration:** Drink plenty of water (dehydration causes fatigue).
- **Avoid burnout:** Take **1 full rest day per week**.

✅ **Test Day Preparation**
- **Check testing center location** (arrive **30 min early**).
- **Valid ID + Authorization to Test (ATT) email** (Print or save on phone).
- **Dress in layers** (testing centers can be cold/hot).
- **Eat a good breakfast** (Protein + carbs for sustained energy).
- **Bring snacks & water** (Granola bars, nuts, bananas).
- **Leave phone, notes, etc. at home** (or in car).
- **Stay calm & confident** – **You’ve prepared for this!**

---
---
### **📝 Sample Daily Study Plan (Example Week)**
| **Day**  | **Morning (3 hrs)** | **Afternoon (2 hrs)** | **Evening (1 hr)** |
|----------|---------------------|-----------------------|-------------------|
| **Mon**  | Pharm (Anticoagulants, Insulin) | 50 UWorld Qs (Pharm focus) | Review incorrect Qs + notes |
| **Tue**  | Med-Surg (Cardiac: MI, HF) | 50 UWorld Qs (Cardiac) | Mark Klimek Pharm Lecture |
| **Wed**  | Maternity (Labor & Delivery) | 50 UWorld Qs (Maternity) | Flashcards (Med-Surg labs) |
| **Thu**  | Delegation & Prioritization | 75 UWorld Qs (Mixed) | Review SATA mistakes |
| **Fri**  | Psych (Schizophrenia, Depression) | 50 UWorld Qs (Psych) | Watch RN Registered Nurse YouTube on ABGs |
| **Sat**  | Full-Length Practice Test (100 Qs) | Review all mistakes | Light review + relax |
| **Sun**  | **REST DAY** (Light flashcards only) | - | - |

---
---
### **⚠️ Common NCLEX Mistakes to Avoid**
❌ **Cramming the night before** → **Review lightly, then sleep!**
❌ **Memorizing without understanding** → **Focus on "why" not just "what."**
❌ **Ignoring SATA & prioritization questions** → **These are HIGH-YIELD!**
❌ **Guessaging on questions** → **Use process of elimination.**
❌ **Not reviewing rationales** → **This is where real learning happens.**
❌ **Skipping practice tests** → **You NEED to simulate test conditions.**
❌ **Overconfidence after a few good scores** → **Stay consistent!**

---
---
### **🎉 Final Tips for Success**
✔ **Be consistent** – Small, daily effort > last-minute cramming.
✔ **Trust the process** – UWorld rationales will make things click.
✔ **Think like a nurse** – **Safety first, then prioritize.**
✔ **Stay positive** – **You’ve passed nursing school; you CAN pass the NCLEX!**
✔ **Take the test when you're scoring 65-75%+ on practice tests.**

---
### **📌 Bonus: Last-Minute Quick Review (Test Day Morning)**
- **ABCs (Airway, Breathing, Circulation)** – Always prioritize!
- **Safety first** (Fall risk, infection control, restraints).
- **Assess before implementing** (Don’t jump to interventions without data).
- **Delegate appropriately** (RN does assessments, CNA does ADLs).
- **Labs:** **K+, Na+, Ca2+, Mg2+, Glucose, ABGs.**
- **Insulin:** **R (Rapid) → Lispro, Aspart, Glulisine | N (Intermediate) → NPH | L (Long) → Glargine, Detemir.**
- **Antidotes:**
  - **Warfarin → Vitamin K**
  - **Heparin → Protamine**
  - **Benzodiazepines → Flumazenil**
  - **Opioids → Naloxone (Narcan)**
  - **Digoxin → Digibind**
  - **Acetaminophen → NAC (Mucomyst)**

---
### **💪 You Got This!**
The NCLEX is **not about memorizing everything**—it’s about **applying nursing knowledge safely and effectively**. Stay disciplined, review consistently, and **trust your gut** on test day.

**Good luck, future RN!** 🩺💉✨
